summary: Zack Beer specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research and the University of California, Berkeley, both attested in 2026.

Zarawar Khan works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi studied under Pe Maung Tin (~1924–1930) at the University of Rangoon (~1924–1929). He later studied at the University of Dublin (~1934–1936).

Zayn Kassam is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. At Pomona College, she was appointed department chair, Associate Dean, and Professor in 1995; she also served at the Institute of Ismaili Studies and directed the Pacific Basin Institute.

Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned a PhD at the University of Michigan in 2001 under Donald S. Lopez Jr., later holding a post at the College of Charleston.
Zellig Harris was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University (~1947–1948).

Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenjo Inoue was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935).

Zenkei Blanche Hartman was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of California (~1943–1947), she trained under Jōshin Kasai, Richard Baker, and Mel Weitsman, later serving as co-abbess at the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).
Zenkei Shibayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Hanazono University (~1948–1967) and Otani University.
Zenno Ikuno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Taisho University (~1949–1956). He held professorial posts at Taisho University (1963–2000), served at Dongguk University, and was president of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014).

Zennosuke Tsuji was a historian of Japan and Buddhism who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1938), University of the Sacred Heart (~1948–1955), and Rissho University (~1949–1954).

Zenryu Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities. He held posts at Kyoto University (1949–1961), Bukkyo University (~1926), Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972), and Kacho Junior College (1973).

Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served at Rissho University as a lecturer (attested 1976) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026), and has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Zesho Machida is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as betto at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and was professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

Zev Handel specializes in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard College (1988) and UC Berkeley (1992, 1998), later becoming a professor at the University of Washington around 2000.
Zhao Luo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (attested 2018).

Zhe Ji works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned a PhD in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and was an associate professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
